reference.title: Incline Push-up
reference.listing: Video; data sheet: body part Chest, equipment Body weight, exercise type Strength
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

breathing.pattern: Inhale as you lower toward the bench, exhale as you press away.
breathing.cadence: About 1.7 s down, short pause, about 1 s up

prescription.progression: Lower surface over the weeks (box, then step, then floor push-up)

cues.text: Hands on the edge of a bench, a little wider than the shoulders, palms flat on top; walk the feet back onto the balls until the body is one straight line.
Breathe in and bend the elbows back at about 45 degrees, bringing the chest toward the edge.
Chest just above the edge of the bench, body still straight.
Breathe out and push the bench away until the arms are straight.
Keep bracing at the top and repeat.

mistakes.fix: Brace the abs and squeeze the glutes so the body stays one straight line from head to heels.
Lower the hips into line with the shoulders and ankles.

mistakes.mistake: Elbows flared straight out to the sides (a "T")
mistakes.fix: Tuck the elbows to about 30-45 degrees from the body, pointing back toward the hips.

mistakes.mistake: Head dropping or chin poking forward
mistakes.fix: Keep the neck long; look at the floor a little ahead of the hands.
Use a stable bench or box against a wall, never a rolling chair.

kinematics.norm: Arms straight but not locked at the top. Many lab protocols standardise the bottom at 90 degrees of elbow flexion (Zhang 2023); lowering the chest to a few cm from the edge of the bench takes the elbows further (clinical opinion)

kinematics.measure: Elbow tuck (upper arm from the trunk)
kinematics.norm: About 30-45 degrees from the body at the bottom (clinical opinion; no measured norm found)
Shoulder width (100% of the acromion distance) or a little wider; 150% raised serratus and lowered pectoralis and triceps activity versus 100% (Kim 2016)
Head, trunk, hips and ankles in one straight line throughout (clinical opinion)
Palms flat; the wrist is bent back about 90 degrees with the forearm vertical (clinical opinion)
Peak hand force about 64% of body mass for a floor push-up, 55% with hands on a 30 cm box and 41% on a 61 cm box (Wurm et al., Ebben lab)
Controlled, about 2 s down and 1 s up; lab studies used 2-2.5 s per repetition (Wurm et al.; Marcolin 2015)

sources.title: Wurm, VanderZanden, Spadavecchia, Durocher, Bickham, Petushek and Ebben, kinetic analysis of several variations of push-ups (ISBS 2010 conference proceedings)

Zhang, Dong, Zhao, Hou, Chen et al. 2023, joint loading and muscle activation of the upper body in incline/decline push-up variants by AnyBody modelling (Research Square preprint rs-3344478, not peer reviewed)
Kim, Kim and Ha 2016, effect of the push-up exercise at different palmar width on muscle activities (J Phys Ther Sci 28(2):446-449; PMC4792988)
Ludewig, Hoff, Osowski, Meschke and Rundquist 2004, relative balance of serratus anterior and upper trapezius muscle activity during push-up exercises (Am J Sports Med 32(2):484-493)

cautions: Wrist pain: the top of a push-up needs about 90 degrees of wrist extension; use push-up handles, fists or a raised surface, or stop if pain persists.
Shoulder pain: keep the elbows tucked (about 30-45 degrees from the body) rather than flared out to the sides, and shorten the range if needed (clinical opinion).
Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Make sure the bench or box is stable and cannot slide or tip.
modify: Wrist pain: grip the edge of the bench with the fingers over the edge, or use push-up handles on the bench.
Use a higher surface (kitchen counter, wall) if the bench is too hard.
regressions: Higher surface (counter or bar in a rack).

muscleNotes.pec_r: Main pusher, at a lower load than the floor push-up: hand force fell from about 64% of body mass on the floor to 55% and 41% with the hands on 30 cm and 61 cm boxes (Wurm et al.); modelled and measured muscle activity also fell as the incline rose (Zhang 2023, preprint).
muscleNotes.pec_l: Main pusher, at a lower load than the floor push-up: hand force fell from about 64% of body mass on the floor to 55% and 41% with the hands on 30 cm and 61 cm boxes (Wurm et al.); modelled and measured muscle activity also fell as the incline rose (Zhang 2023, preprint).
muscleNotes.triceps_r: Straightens the elbows on the way up and brakes the elbows on the way down; more active with narrower hands (Kim 2016; Marcolin 2015).
muscleNotes.triceps_l: Straightens the elbows on the way up and brakes the elbows on the way down; more active with narrower hands (Kim 2016; Marcolin 2015).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Flexes the shoulder with the chest muscles; hand width made little difference to it (Kim 2016; Marcolin 2015).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Flexes the shoulder with the chest muscles; hand width made little difference to it (Kim 2016; Marcolin 2015).
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Holds the shoulder blades on the rib cage and spreads them at the top; the push-up plus gave the highest serratus activity of the push-up variants tested (Ludewig 2004), and it was higher with wider hands (Kim 2016).
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Holds the shoulder blades on the rib cage and spreads them at the top; the push-up plus gave the highest serratus activity of the push-up variants tested (Ludewig 2004), and it was higher with wider hands (Kim 2016).
muscleNotes.core: Bracing keeps the hips from sagging or piking: the body moves as one plank.
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Help hold the trunk rigid and level.
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Help hold the trunk rigid and level.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Control the shoulder blades as they draw together on the way down.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_l: Control the shoulder blades as they draw together on the way down.
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_r: Keeps the head of the upper arm centred as the elbows bend.
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_l: Keeps the head of the upper arm centred as the elbows bend.
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Squeezed lightly to keep the pelvis in line (no sag).
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Squeezed lightly to keep the pelvis in line (no sag).
muscleNotes.quads_r: Keep the knees straight so the legs stay part of the plank.
muscleNotes.quads_l: Keep the knees straight so the legs stay part of the plank.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Hold a long, neutral spine and neck.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Hold a long, neutral spine and neck.

phases.label: Hands on the bench, body straight
